restoration_note: This teaching describes the Father of Greatness in his inmost articulation (five members = the five intellectual faculties; twelve members = the twelve Wisdoms) and the procession of five attributes (Light, Fragrance, Voice, …, …) into all the aeons. The first half is well constrained: the canonical five-faculty list, the 'aeons of the Greatness' formula (parallel between sections 1218–1220), and the rhythmic 'first/second/third/fourth/fifth is his X' structure all admit confident or moderate fills. Editor restorations of small grammatical fragments (suffixes, copulas, completions of ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ, ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ, etc.) are confirmed. The second half (sections 1223–1234) is too fragmentary: the 4th and 5th attributes, the ⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁϥⲉ verb, ⲕⲟⲛⲟⲣⲡⲁϥⲓⲁ, and the multiple short lacunae describing the sealing-nourishing-renewing operations cannot be restored without invention, and are honestly marked unrestorable.
